facts.summary: New Hampshire has no daily overtime and no higher salary floor; overtime is paid at 1.5x the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a week, tracking the federal FLSA.
facts.notes: RSA 279:21 expressly ties overtime to the FLSA (over 40 hours/week at time and one-half); no state daily-OT or higher salary threshold.

facts.summary: New Hampshire pegs its minimum wage to the federal minimum wage, so the 2026 rate is $7.25 per hour.
facts.notes: RSA 279:21 sets the wage at 'the federal minimum wage law, as amended.' Confirm $7.25 remains the federal rate for 2026.

facts.summary: Tipped employees who regularly receive more than $30/month in tips may be paid a cash wage of no less than $3.27/hour, provided tips plus cash wage meet the full minimum wage.
facts.notes: State-specific tip credit figure; employer must make up any shortfall so total pay reaches the applicable minimum wage.

facts.summary: Beyond the federal protected classes, New Hampshire's Law Against Discrimination also prohibits employment discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity, and marital status.
facts.notes: Full state list also covers age, sex (incl. pregnancy), race, color, disability, religious creed, and national origin; the values here are the additions beyond the federal Title VII/ADA/ADEA set.

facts.summary: New Hampshire's anti-discrimination law covers employers with 6 or more employees, a lower threshold than the federal 15-employee minimum under Title VII.
facts.notes: Statute excludes 'any employer with fewer than 6 persons in its employ,' so coverage begins at 6 employees.

facts.summary: A discrimination complaint must be filed with the New Hampshire Commission for Human Rights within 180 days after the alleged discriminatory act.
facts.notes: State FEPA (Commission for Human Rights) filing deadline is 180 days; a related superior court civil action must be brought within 3 years of the act.

facts.summary: New Hampshire's Whistleblowers' Protection Act bars employers from discharging or discriminating against employees who in good faith report, or refuse to participate in, a suspected violation of law or rule.
facts.notes: Enforced by the NH Department of Labor; complaints filed on the DOL Whistleblowers' Complaint Form.

facts.value: discharge: 72 hours; quit: next regular payday
facts.summary: A discharged employee must be paid in full within 72 hours; an employee who quits must be paid by the next regular payday (or within 72 hours if they gave at least one pay period's notice).
facts.notes: Layoff/suspension pay is due no later than the next regular payday. Wage claims are enforced by the NH DOL Wage and Hour Bureau.

facts.summary: A New Hampshire wage claim, whether filed by the employee or by the Department of Labor, must be filed no later than 36 months (3 years) from the date the wages were due.
facts.notes: RSA 275:51 states a wage claim 'may be filed by an employee or by the department on its own motion no later than 36 months from the date the wages were due.' This is the administrative wage-claim filing deadline with the NH Department of Labor; a private civil action may be subject to a different period.
